issues.spec_reference: spec.tex l.2182: "The original model is not changed; a failed completion does not stop the solve."
issues.location: src/fleet_management/degradation_model/base.py, complete_binary_warm_start, lines 488-517 (fixed.optimize(), fixed.computeIIS(), getConstrs/getGenConstrs); the call at solve_mixed lines 1351-1353
issues.description: The spec says a failed completion never stops the solve. The code handles the statuses (infeasible, infeasible_or_unbounded, time_limit, status_q), but it has no try/except around the copy, the optimisation of the copy or computeIIS. A gurobipy.GurobiError in any of them (for example computeIIS on a model type or state it cannot handle, or a failure of model.copy()) leaves complete_binary_warm_start, and therefore solve(); in a sweep it becomes a case error. The copy is also not disposed on that path (fixed.dispose() is at line 519, not in a finally). The tests pass because Gurobi did not fail on the tested inputs.
issues.suggested_fix: Either wrap the body after the copy in try/except gurobipy.GurobiError, record the status (for example "error") and dispose in a finally, and add the new status to the table of l.1851; or state in the spec at l.2182 that only the listed statuses are survived and that a Gurobi exception is raised.

issues.spec_reference: spec.tex l.2077-2082 (arguments of sweep_horizon_grid) and l.2092-2095 (Errors: only "ValueError: evaluation_horizon, if given, does not exceed every H1"); l.2079 "output_path ... Report file of the grid"; l.2082 "The keyword arguments of sweep_operating_horizons except objective_mode"
issues.location: src/fleet_management/horizon_sweep.py, sweep_horizon_grid lines 875-886 and 893-904; _positive_integers lines 123-131; _check_output_path lines 566-574; _check_sweep_arguments lines 598-667
issues.description: The grid raises more errors than the spec lists. (a) An empty transitory_horizons or operating_horizons list gives ValueError (_positive_integers: "must contain at least one value"); the grid arguments say only "positive integers" and the at-least-one rule is stated for the operating sweep only (l.1934). (b) output_path must end in .yaml or .yml (ValueError, line 571); l.2079 has no rule for the grid, l.1935 has it for the operating sweep. (c) objective_mode inside sweep_options gives ValueError (lines 877-880); in Python an unknown keyword would give TypeError, and the spec does not say which. (d) any other unknown option gives TypeError from _check_sweep_arguments. (e) the sweep-option checks (gradient_tolerance, minimum_cases, n_workers, warm_start with n_workers>1, ...) run for every H1 before the first case; the grid Errors table lists none of them. (f) The grid does not check the shape of H in the input (a list of length not two), because H is overwritten in every case; the operating sweep does check it (l.1961).
issues.suggested_fix: In the grid Errors table add: ValueError for an empty or invalid list, for an output_path that is not .yaml/.yml, for objective_mode among the options, and for any invalid sweep option (as in the operating sweep); TypeError for an unknown option. State that the grid does not read H of the input.

issues.spec_reference: spec.tex l.1991-2002 (stop rule) and l.2021 (stopping_rule.reason: "in_progress", "candidate_range_exhausted", "cost_increase" or "flat_gradient"; stopped_early: "complete with fewer cases than planned"); l.2002 "The last candidate of operating_horizons is a hard limit."
issues.description: The code tests the stop rule after every case, also after the last candidate. When the rule fires at the last candidate, the loop ends because the list is exhausted, but stopping_reason is "cost_increase" or "flat_gradient" and the report gives that reason with stopped_early = false. The spec gives reason "candidate_range_exhausted" no condition and does not say what the reason is when the stop rule and the end of the list coincide. A reader of the spec can expect "candidate_range_exhausted" there. No test is likely to cover it (it needs the rule to fire exactly at the last candidate).
issues.suggested_fix: Add to the stop rule or to the key stopping_rule: "If the stop rule holds after the last candidate, reason is the reason of the rule and stopped_early is false" (current code), or change the code to report "candidate_range_exhausted" when no candidate is left.

issues.spec_reference: spec.tex l.2153 "The mapped values, rounded to the nearest integer, are:"; l.2174 "Time limit: completion_time_limit of the source (seconds, default 60)."; l.2178 "fix every binary variable that has a Start value to that value"
issues.description: (a) Rounding uses Python round(), which rounds a tie to the even integer (0.5 -> 0, 1.5 -> 2). The spec does not state the tie rule. The rounded value is not limited to {0,1}: a source value of 1.5 or 2 sets Start = 2 on a binary variable, and the completion then fixes the variable with lower and upper bound 2 (which makes the copy infeasible). The spec says nothing about values outside [0,1]. (b) completion_time_limit is not validated: None gives TypeError from float(None), a negative value is passed to Gurobi, and the spec states only a default of 60. (c) The completion fixes variables of type BINARY or INTEGER; the spec says "binary" (equal for the present model, which has no general integer variable).
issues.suggested_fix: Add to l.2153 "a tie goes to the even integer; a value outside {0,1} is used as it is", or clip to {0,1} in the code. Add to l.2174 the rule for an invalid completion_time_limit (accepted or ValueError).

issues.spec_reference: spec.tex l.1808 ("model_construction_seconds: Model construction"); l.2178-2182 and l.2195-2196 (completion and relaxation copies); l.1858-1867 (report relaxation_warm_start)
issues.location: src/fleet_management/degradation_model/base.py, solve_mixed lines 1347-1369 (construction_seconds); complete_binary_warm_start lines 482-484 (copy silenced); apply_relaxation_warm_start lines 545-553 (copy not silenced)
issues.description: (a) model_construction_seconds is measured from before build_fleet to after the warm-start phases, so it includes the mapping, the completion (up to 60 s) and the relaxation (at least 1 s); the spec calls the entry "Model construction". (b) The completion copy is silenced (OutputFlag 0, LogToConsole 0, LogFile ""), but the relaxation copy is not: its Gurobi log goes to the console and, through the copied parameters, to the LogFile of the run. The spec states neither. (c) Both copies inherit every parameter of the original (MIPGap, Threads, Seed, NonConvex, gurobi_params); the spec states only the parameters it overrides (TimeLimit, and MIPGap 0.05 for the relaxation).
issues.suggested_fix: State in l.1808 that model_construction_seconds includes the warm-start phases (or measure them apart), and in the sections of the completion and the relaxation which parameters the copy takes from the original and whether it writes a log.

issues.location: src/fleet_management/degradation_model/base.py, apply_binary_warm_start line 358; complete_binary_warm_start lines 451-458; solve_mixed lines 1354-1360
issues.description: The reports give a value for every key also when the mechanism does not run, and the spec states only part of them: completion.runtime_seconds is null while the completion does not run (the table says "Runtime of the completion, in seconds"); relaxation_warm_start.runtime_seconds and relaxation_objective are null when disabled, skipped, or when the copy has no solution (relaxation_objective only if the copy has a solution is not stated, the table says "Objective value of the relaxed copy"); relaxation_warm_start.values_copied is 0 then; with a source that has no x the report is applied=false, values=0, mode=null, source_horizon=null, the same as without a source (the spec: mode "null without a source").
issues.suggested_fix: Add a line to each report table: the entries that belong to a step that did not run are null (runtime_seconds, relaxation_objective) or 0 (counts), and a source without x is reported as no source.

issues.spec_reference: spec.tex l.2259 "for \"pwl\" the cap of the segment that contains the mean of the day (...; the last segment for a mean above tau)"; l.2223 "r = repair_trigger must lie in [0,1]"; l.2244 "The check F > M ... guarantees a train for every mission"
issues.description: (a) For a negative mean the code clips the mean to 0 and uses the first segment, with the tangent evaluated at the unclipped mean; the spec fixes only the case above tau. (b) repair_trigger: NaN raises the ValueError (correct), but a non-number raises TypeError, and a bool is accepted as 0 or 1. (c) If F <= M reaches the greedy without the input check (a cfg built by hand), min() of an empty list raises ValueError with an unclear message. These are rare inputs (a negative mean cannot occur after the input checks), so the effect is small.
issues.suggested_fix: Optional: add to l.2259 "first segment for a mean below 0"; no code change needed.
